sources.citation: Hanna, Roger & Leanne Hanna. 1991. Phonology of Napu. In René van den Berg (ed.), Sulawesi phonologies (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 12), 150-178. Ujung Pandang: UNHAS-SIL.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: About NAPU, the sister Badaic language, not Besoa: section 4 Stress (p. 156) 'Stress is not phonemic. It occurs on the penultimate syllable of the word, except when a post-clitic is attached'; stress stays on the root's penult before post-clitics and moves to the penult of the whole word with suffixes. Besoa is mentioned only in the introduction (Besoa and Bada have the glottal stop and a sixth vowel).

sources.note: SILENT. Bab II Fonologi (pp. 9-17) has only 2.1 Fonem Segmental: 2.1.1 vowels (5) and diphthongs (5), 2.1.2 consonants (15 incl. glottal stop), 2.1.3 distribution tables, 2.1.4 Struktur Fonemis (prenasalised clusters mb mp nd nt ng nk); the chapter ends at p. 17 (verified on page images) and 5.1 Fonologi (p. 64) repeats the same four segmental points. No tekanan/aksen/intonasi/suprasegmental section; a full-text search for stress/accent the full scanned text for tekanan|aksen|intonasi|suprasegmen|penultima|nada returns nothing. downloaded from the the Internet Archive 2023-05-31 capture of re…
No phonology; cites only Ethnologue, Martens 1989 and Saro et al. 1991.

sources.citation: Martens, Michael P. 1989. The Badaic languages of Central Sulawesi. In James N. Sneddon (ed.), Studies in Sulawesi languages, part 1 (NUSA 31), 19-53. Jakarta: Universitas Katolik Indonesia Atma Jaya.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Comparative survey: Bada, Besoa (locally Behoa) and Napu form a tight subgroup; phoneme charts (glottal stop contrastive in Besoa and Bada, absent in Napu), pronoun/clitic charts, lexicostatistics, 200-item wordlist. The only 'accent' mention is sociolinguistic (Besoa speakers speak Bada or Napu 'with no accent').
